chips: Keloid risk in skin of colour

points.t: Depressions or raised scars after inflammatory acne; patients often call **flat pigment** ‘scarring’ too.
**Collagen destruction** (atrophic) or **excess collagen** (hypertrophic, or keloid beyond the borders).
**Control active acne first**, then specialist modalities matched to scar type, with realistic expectations.
Scarring at **any** acne severity is an NG198 referral trigger; distress; keloid tendency before procedures.

cause.lead: Too little collagen, or too much.
points: Inflammatory nodules and cysts destroy collagen → **atrophic** scars (ice-pick, boxcar, rolling).
Excess collagen → **hypertrophic** (within the lesion) or **keloid** (spreads **beyond** the original border).
Risk rises with severity, duration, **picking** and smoking; keloids and PIH commoner in **skin of colour**.
**PIE / PIH** are colour change, not scars.

visuals.caption: Atrophic scar types: ice-pick (narrow, deeper than wide), boxcar (sharp vertical walls, flat base) and rolling (broad sloping wave tethered by fibrous bands).
visuals.alt: Three skin sections of ice-pick, boxcar and rolling scars

features.lead: Name the scar type: it decides the treatment.
points: **Ice-pick**: narrow, deep, V-shaped (60–70% of atrophic); cheeks.
**Boxcar**: round or oval, sharp vertical edges; cheeks, temples.
**Rolling**: wide, sloping, tethered by dermal bands; cheeks.
**Perifollicular elastolysis**: small pale follicular scars; back, chest.
**Hypertrophic**: raised, same size as lesion. **Keloid**: beyond the border; shoulders, chest, jawline, earlobes.

visuals.caption: Hypertrophic scar (left) stays inside the original wound outline; a keloid (right) spreads beyond it, with thick swirled collagen. Keloids recur often after excision.
visuals.alt: Skin sections comparing hypertrophic scar and keloid

items.name: PIH, not scar
items.t: Flat colour change in skin of colour.

points: **Fitzpatrick type**, acne still active?, patient goals.
Rarely: only an atypical or evolving ‘keloid’.

cards.name: PIH / erythema alone
cards.clue: Flat colour, no depression or elevation.

cards.name: Dermatofibroma or tumour
cards.clue: Solitary atypical nodule mimicking a keloid: refer.

manage.lead: Prevent by treating acne early; scar treatment is specialist and multi-session.

points: Treat active acne **early and adequately**; scarring = refer (NG198); clear acne before procedures.
**Silicone gel or sheet** (OTC) for months, not weeks.
Ice-pick: TCA CROSS, punch excision / grafting.
Boxcar: fractional laser, peels, punch, microneedling.
Intralesional steroid, pulsed dye laser, cryotherapy, careful revision (**high recurrence**).

limits.t: Higher PIH and keloid risk: experienced operator only.

items.t: Scarring or significant distress at any acne severity (NG198).
Rapidly growing or atypical ‘keloid’: exclude a tumour.
Low mood, anxiety or body dysmorphic concerns: mental-health support.

pearls.t: Silicone gel for months for early raised scars.
This page is counselling and recognition, not a procedure how-to.

quiz.a: Keloid extends beyond the original wound; hypertrophic stays within it.

quiz.q: OTC first step for an early raised scar?
quiz.a: Silicone gel or sheet, used for months.
